youtube.title: Tardigrades in Space: The Animal That Survived the Void
youtube.description:
Tardigrades in space: in 2007, scientists strapped dried water bears to the outside of a satellite. How did a tiny animal survive the open void?

On the FOTON-M3 mission, the TARDIS experiment left dried tardigrades in the vacuum of low Earth orbit for about ten days, some also under raw solar ultraviolet light. Back on Earth, a drop of water revived many of them, although most of the ones hit by full sunlight died. The secret is the tun: a dried tardigrade pulls in its legs and its body almost stops. Researchers led by Ingemar Jonsson reported it in 2008.

Subscribe to Stickstory for a strange true story every day. Would you send a water bear to Mars? Tell me in the comments!

#shorts #tardigrades #waterbear #stickstory

scenes.text: This tiny animal survived open space.
scenes.visual: A huge cute tardigrade (plump segmented body, round head with a snout ring, eight stubby clawed legs) floats paddling among ink stars above a flat Earth horizon; the big fez narrator stands on the horizon at the left looking up through binoculars, then jumps back in shock on 'space'.

scenes.text: Meet the tardigrade, the water bear.
scenes.visual: The fez narrator on the right holds a giant magnifying glass; inside the lens a tardigrade walks over moss among drifting water bubbles, a '0.5 mm' scale bar draws under it, 'WATER BEAR' is handwritten at the top of the lens on 'water'.

scenes.text: In 2007, scientists dried some and strapped them to a satellite.
scenes.visual: Close-up of the FOTON capsule in space (sphere with a hatch, service cylinder, antennas); on its outside an open experiment box holds a tray of six dried tuns, two brown straps run down over the tray on 'strapped'; a handwritten red '10 DAYS' note pops in at the top right.

scenes.text: Back on Earth, they added water. Here's the crazy part: many woke up!
scenes.visual: A lab bench with flasks on a shelf; a dropper with a red bulb lets one blue drop fall into a glass dish with a dried tun on 'water'; in a big round close-up the wrinkled tun swells, stretches its eight legs and starts walking; a green 'ALIVE!' box pops in on 'woke'; the fez narrator jumps back in shock.

scenes.text: Raw sunlight killed most, but a few made it.
scenes.visual: A gold ink sun blazes at the top right; three red zig-zag ultraviolet rays shoot into the open tray on the capsule and the tuns flash red; a red 'MOST DIED' pops in, then a green box 'A FEW LIVED' on 'few'.
Giant Fraunces words slam in: 'WHY DID THEY', then 'LIVE?' in a red box on its own line; the fez narrator at the lower right rubs his chin, thinking.

scenes.text: Dried out, it pulls in its legs and becomes a tiny barrel.
scenes.visual: Inside the giant magnifying glass the walking tardigrade stops, pulls in its eight legs and its head and shrivels into a wrinkled dry barrel (a 'tun'); a red 'TUN' box stamps in on 'barrel'; the fez narrator holding the lens leans in curiously, then jumps back in shock.

scenes.text: Its body nearly stops, like pausing your life.
scenes.visual: The dried tun rests on a line; above it a heart monitor's beating red trace slows and flattens into rare tiny blips, a small heart icon beats slower; on 'pause' the fez narrator presses a big red pause button, a blue 'PAUSED' box stamps in and little 'z' letters float up from the tun.

scenes.text: It didn't beat space by being tough.
scenes.visual: The tardigrade floats among the stars above a thin Earth horizon; a big 'TOUGH' appears and the fez narrator points up at it, then on 'tough' it is struck through with a red line and he shrugs.

scenes.text: It beat space by switching itself off.
scenes.visual: The floating tardigrade pulls in its legs and curls into a dry tun in mid-space on 'switching'; the fez narrator on the horizon points down and presses a big red power button on 'off' (it sinks) while a red 'OFF' stamp slams in above the tun.
